samples.summary: Two `outputError` call sites were not converted, so `ctx list` and `status` emit envelopes with no `command`
samples.evidence: The change's contract is that every error envelope carries the dotted command name (`outputError(e, this)` was added at ~40 sites). Two sites were missed: `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:85` (`outputError(e);` in `ctx list`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:69` (`outputError(e);` in `status`). Because `errorEnvelope` omits `command` when it is falsy, an agent gets `{code:'NOT_LOGGED_IN',message:...}` with no attribution from `ctx list` but `{...,command:'ctx.switch'}` from `ctx switch` — exactly the per-subcommand divergence the new comment in `ctx switch` (lines 97-101) says must not happen. Grep of `packages/cli/src` shows these are the only remaining un-attributed `outputError` calls.

samples.summary: `cliLoginAvailable()` treats an unset `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` as non-loopback, so a non-production install with the documented-optional variable omitted can no longer run `wafflebase login`
samples.evidence: `callbackHost()` returns `undefined` when `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is empty, so `loopbackCallback()` is `false`, and with `NODE_ENV!=='production'` and no `COOKIE_SECURE`, `useSecureCookies()` is `false` too — `cliLoginAvailable()` returns `false` and `assertCliLoginAvailable()` throws `BadRequestException('Command-line sign-in requires an https server…')`. `docs/design/backend.md:764` documents `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` as *not required* (Required = No) and `github.strategy.ts:46` passes `configService.get(...)!` through as `undefined` on purpose, so this is a supported configuration; a developer running `pnpm start:dev` on localhost without that env var is now told to serve over https even though the origin is loopback. The refusal is deliberate per the docblock, but it is decided by the *absence* of config rather than by the origin, so the loopback exemption the same docblock relies on does not apply to the most common local setup.
searchedFor: grep GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL across repo (README, docs/design/backend.md, github.strategy.ts, integration-helpers.ts)

samples.summary: The new loopback→backend 302 makes the CLI start URL arrive via a cross-origin redirect, which the backend's `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate may see as `cross-site` and 400
samples.evidence: `await deps.openBrowser(armLaunch(oauthUrl))` now hands the browser `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<token>`, which 302s to `<server>/auth/github?mode=cli…`. `GitHubAuthGuard.assertCliStartNotCrossSite` (github-auth.guard.ts:309-319) refuses any CLI start whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is not `none`/`same-origin`/`same-site`. The Fetch Metadata spec keeps `none` for a UA-initiated navigation across the redirect chain, so this should hold, but the guard's own doc assumed the CLI navigates directly ("`none` — … `wafflebase login` hands the URL to the OS opener"), and any browser that recomputes the header per redirect hop (initiator 127.0.0.1 vs the backend origin) would answer `cross-site` and 400 every CLI login. Nothing in the changed test suites drives a redirected navigation against the guard, so the assumption is unverified.
searchedFor: read startCallbackServer /launch handler and runLogin call site

samples.summary: The single-use launch link is consumed by any dereference (opener probe, link scanner, prefetch), turning a normal login into a 410 that requires Ctrl-C and a re-run
samples.evidence: `if (isOurToken && launchTarget) { launchTarget = undefined; … }` spends the token on the *first* GET, whoever makes it. Some system openers/browsers probe or pre-resolve a URL before displaying it, and any such request now takes the redirect away from the real browser; the user then sees `SPENT_LAUNCH_PAGE` (410) and, per that page, must Ctrl-C and re-run `wafflebase login`. Recovery only works because `announceLoginUrl(oauthUrl)` still exposes the (non-single-use) authorization URL, so the failure is a usability regression rather than a dead end — but the previous code had no way to lose the login this way.
searchedFor: read startCallbackServer launch branch and SPENT_LAUNCH_PAGE

samples.summary: `res.writeHead(302, { Location: target })` can throw synchronously inside the request handler for a malformed `--server`, taking the CLI down
samples.evidence: `target` is `launchTarget`, i.e. `${server}/auth/github?…` built from the user-supplied `--server` / config value without validation (validation happens later, in `fetchOrThrow`). A value containing a CR/LF or other invalid header character makes `writeHead` throw `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` inside the `createServer` request callback, which is an uncaught exception rather than a reported login failure. Before this change the URL was only passed to `open()`, where the same input could not crash the process.
searchedFor: read runLogin oauthUrl construction (server from options.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER)
read startCallbackServer launch redirect writeHead call

finding.summary: The new loopback→backend 302 makes the CLI start URL arrive via a cross-origin redirect, which the backend's `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate may see as `cross-site` and 400
finding.evidence: `await deps.openBrowser(armLaunch(oauthUrl))` now hands the browser `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<token>`, which 302s to `<server>/auth/github?mode=cli…`. `GitHubAuthGuard.assertCliStartNotCrossSite` (github-auth.guard.ts:309-319) refuses any CLI start whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is not `none`/`same-origin`/`same-site`. The Fetch Metadata spec keeps `none` for a UA-initiated navigation across the redirect chain, so this should hold, but the guard's own doc assumed the CLI navigates directly ("`none` — … `wafflebase login` hands the URL to the OS opener"), and any browser that recomputes the header per redirect hop (initiator 127.0.0.1 vs the backend origin) would answer `cross-site` and 400 every CLI login. Nothing in the changed test suites drives a redirected navigation against the guard, so the assumption is unverified.
searchedFor: read startCallbackServer /launch handler and runLogin call site

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (armLaunch returns http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<token> at login.ts:826-830, answered with a 302 to the backend CLI start URL at login.ts:658-670; the guard refuses non-allowed Sec-Fetch-Site at github-auth.guard.ts:309-319), but the claimed breakage does not occur. The guard's allow-list already includes `none` (github-auth.guard.ts:129) and its doc explicitly covers the "opened by another program" shape (lines 281-283). Fetch Metadata assigns `none` per hop whenever the request has no initiator, which is exactly the case for an OS-opener-launched navigation and every redirect hop of it — the finding concedes this. No path in this flow gives the navigation a loopback initiator origin: the 302 is header-only with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer (line 667), the spent-launch response is a static page with no link (lines 470-497), and the human fallback announces the backend oauthUrl directly rather than the launch URL (line 355), so a pasted URL is also initiator-less. An absent/blank header also returns early (line 311, tested at github-auth.guard.spec.ts:286-295). What is left is a hypothetical non-conforming UA (none named) plus a test-coverage gap, which is not a correctness defect under this lens.

mergedFrom.summary: `openBrowser` attaches the child `error` listener too late to catch a failed spawn

finding.summary: `openBrowser` attaches the child `error` listener after `await`, which may be too late to prevent an uncaught exception

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim (login.ts:121-122), but the claimed uncaught-exception path is based on inverted event-loop ordering. `spawn()` is reached only after `await import('open')` (login.ts:120), i.e. from inside a microtask, so the `process.nextTick(onErrorNT, ...)` that `child_process.spawn` schedules is queued *during* a microtask drain. Node's processTicksAndRejections drains the whole microtask queue — including jobs enqueued during the drain — before returning to the tick queue (`Promise.resolve().then(() => process.nextTick(a)).then(b)` runs b before a). Under the reviewer's own reading of open v11 (`spawn(); unref(); return subprocess;` with no intervening await), the `await` resumption that installs the listener at login.ts:122 is queued in that same drain and therefore runs before `onErrorNT`, so the emitter always has an 'error' listener when the event fires. The only alternative — open awaiting something tick-yielding between spawn and return — requires open to hold its own synchronous `once('error', reject)`/`events.once`, in which case the failure arrives as a rejection handled by the try/catch at login.ts:119-125 (exactly the mechanism the doc comment at login.ts:103-113 describes). Both branches are absorbed; there is no crash path. The proposed fix (`open(url).then(c => c?.on?.('error', ...))`) is tick-ordering-identical to the current code, further indicating the premise is wrong. The weaker point about the test (login-callback.test.ts:177-186 emitting after return) is test-strength, not a runtime correctness defect, and belongs to the test lens.
